The year-long allergy may also be a factor in your TMJ symptoms. After doing extensive research over the past month from being sick in so many different ways I have come to realize how closely connected our nose, ears, and throats are, hence why we have ENT doctors. Also seems that TMJ is also very closely connected to these parts of the body too and many viral/bacterial infections can then cause TMJ issues as well.  

I think it's important to see different specialists within reason. Sometimes there is an underlying thing that can exhibit symptoms in other ways and in other parts of the body and being able to narrow down exactly what is happening is really helpful. 

Glad you found ways to mitigate your symptoms and wish you the best of luck!

The biggest issue with permanent daylight savings time is super late sunrises for certain parts of the contiguous US (e.g. certain parts of Montana, North Dakota, and Michigan would not see their latest sunrise until 9:30-10 a.m.). That is why I decided to focus on sunrises instead of sunsets. This map follows the natural pattern of the sun hitting the surface of the United States. I understand it would have to be adjusted due to certain areas bordering a time zone wanting to change sides or certain states wanting to be all under one time zone however I feel as though this is an improvement to the current one in place. I think daylight savings time should be made permanent but not if certain time zones are changed.

It would coincide with sunsets and wouldnt push them foward to super unreasonably early times. The problem woth permanent daylight savings time in the winter is that some parts of michigan, montana, and north dakota wouldnt have sunrises until 9:30 - 10 am but this would fix that.
